title: The k most frequent elements
summary: Tally every song request, then pick the k songs requested most, without sorting every song.
goal: Name the k songs requested most often

mapping.formal: k values with the highest counts

examples.label: Six requests, k = 2
examples.explanation: Song 1 was requested 3 times and song 2 twice.

examples.label: One request
examples.explanation: The only song is the top song.

ladder.name: Count, then sort every song
ladder.idea: Tally requests per song, sort all songs by their tally, and take the first k.

ladder.name: Count, then keep a heap of k
ladder.idea: Tally requests, then keep the k most-requested songs in a min-heap ordered by count.
ladder.insight: We need only the top k, not the full order, so a heap of size k is enough.

ladder.name: Count, then shelve by count
ladder.idea: Tally requests, then place each song on a shelf numbered by its count. Read shelves from the highest number down until k songs are collected.
ladder.insight: Counts are whole numbers between 1 and n, so songs can be placed directly by count, which is a sort without comparisons.

transfer.problem: Find the 3 words used most often in a long document.
transfer.explanation: Count each word with a map, then pick the top 3 counts with a small heap or with buckets by count.

selfCheck: Counts every request with a map.
Never sorts all songs when buckets or a heap will do.
The examples have no ties for the k-th place.
